messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: realtime p99 latency > 1200ms for /v1/stream in eu-west-1 (30m window). Trigger: latency_regression_detector. Paging @oncall-maya. Dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/streaming-latency?orgId=1

oncall-maya: On it. Paging SREs and infra. Quick checklist: region routing, recent deploys, KV cache hitrate, autoscaler.

sre-alex: Checking deploys — no prod deploys in the last 2h. Looking at node saturation and evictions.

eng-dmitri: Pulling proxy + gateway tails now. Running: `kubectl -n prod logs -l app=rt-proxy --since=20m | grep -i latency`

prod-ella: Customer impact: support funnel shows a spike in user-visible timeouts for EU streaming customers. Any ETA on scope?

support-john: Confirming from ticket aggregator: ~12 distinct user-facing errors in eu-west-1 in the last 15m, correlated to long-lived streaming flows.

oncall-maya: Quick checks results: 1) KV cache hitrate dropped from ~92% -> ~45% at 12:14UTC 2) p95 jumped first, then p99. Looks correlated with KV misses. Can we apply a fallback config?

sre-alex: Eviction metrics spiking — evictions/instance up ~6x. Running `./scripts/kv-stats.sh --region eu-west-1` to gather details.

eng-dmitri: Proxy mem usage spike observed on rt-proxy-5, not OOMed yet. Recommend scaling pods to reduce per-pod cache pressure. Executing: `kubectl -n prod scale deployment/rt-proxy --replicas=6`

opsbot: deploy-bot: autoscaler override applied by oncall-maya -> set minReplicas=6 for rt-proxy (eu-west-1)

oncall-maya: Scaling in flight. Also enabling prefix cache warmup fallback for streaming routes. Patch applied: `PATCH /configs/cache/fallback {"enabled":true,"ttl":30s}`

prod-ella: Notified affected beta customers with an interim message; tracking responses in #customer-notify.

support-john: Draft customer update: "We're investigating degraded streaming performance in EU. Engineers applied mitigations and are monitoring—next update in 15m." Approve to send?

sre-alex: :thumbsup: Send it.

eng-dmitri: Post-scale metrics: p95 dropped from ~880ms -> ~240ms within 4 minutes. p99 reduced but is ~720ms still. KV hitrate recovering to ~78%.

oncall-maya: Good progress. Keep 30m watch. If p99 > 500ms again, plan: failover heavy streaming routing to eu-central fallback region and keep bridge open.

incident-bot: incident-bot: Incident bridge created -> https://zoom.redwood.example/bridge/6401234567. Incident ID INC-2026-045

prod-ella: Follow-ups assigned: probable root cause = KV eviction threshold too aggressive under recent prefix churn. Owner: eng-dmitri. Action-items: increase cache size, add eviction-rate alert, and add warmup for new prefixes.

sre-alex: I'll open a runbook PR: `github.com/redwood/runbooks/rt-kv-eviction` with step-by-step mitigation and rollback notes.

support-john: Customer note sent, monitoring incoming tickets and escalation channel.

oncall-maya: Final check: p99 stabilized ~230ms, error counts back to baseline. Marking incident as mitigated for now — bridge remains open for 1h for verification. Closing paging.
